Sentence (English): Purchased this dishwasher after our Bosch (12+ years old) dishwasher broke and was no longer economically feasible to repair and so far have been extremely pleased with the Kitchenaid dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Purchased this dishwasher after our Bosch (12+ years old) dishwasher broke and was no longer economically feasible to repair and so far have been extremely pleased with the Kitchenaid dishwasher. I was originally leaning toward purchasing another Bosch because of my past experience and reputation, but it was the design of the third rack in the Kitchenaid dishwasher that ultimately swayed me to make a change. The FreeFlex Third Rack is a clever design that goes beyond most current third rack designs and actually provides a tangible benefit when loading the dishwasher. Granted, the third rack can fill up quickly, but it is still a better use of space than the traditional flat third racks in my opinion. Another important factor in my purchase decision was the noise level. I thought my old Bosch was quiet, but it had nothing on this Kitchenaid! Granted, it had been more than 12 years since I purchased a dishwasher and maybe the current noise level is standard, but I really enjoy how quiet this dishwasher is.Aesthetically, the dishwasher is a very nice unit and matches other appliances well. The controls are intuitive and I appreciate this unit has a drying setting as many of the current dishwashers seem to be doing away with that feature. Overall, we are extremely pleased with the dishwasher. It looks very nice, makes great use of the interior space with the FreeFlex Third Rack, and cleans well while doing so quietly!

Sentence (English): I can't tell you how many YouTube videos I searched before buying a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ It's kind of convenient ] || ---------------- || I can't tell you how many YouTube videos I searched before buying a dishwasher. Since I knew I'd be using it for a long time, I read reviews very carefully. I agonized over whether to go with SK or LG. I noticed other brands would get damp and drip down the sides, which I thought was a chronic problem with those brands, so I decided to go with LG. The LG's strengths were its soaking function, high-pressure washing, high-temperature drying, and water softening. Today, I used it without the water softening function. I wiped all the food off the dishes first, and the pots, plates, lids, and other items at the bottom cleaned very well, but the rice in the middle was dried and not peeling off. The spoons were clean, but the dried food on the cooking utensils was still there. And, perhaps because it wasn't using the water softening function, it had water stains. Anyway, not having to stand for 30 minutes to wash dishes is incredibly convenient. That alone makes me feel good about buying it. Next time, I'll be more thorough and arrange the dishes better! ^^ I had a lot of concerns about the color, so I'm uploading this for your reference~. Added). Oh, I just noticed that the newer models have a frying pan hanger. This one doesn't. Is that because it's an older model? And after using it a few times, this white residue remains. Other regular dishes are transparent or white, so it doesn't show up well, but the frying pan shows it clearly. Judging from the fact that it washes clean with water, I don't think it's limescale. Could it be detergent residue or salt from the water softener? If it's salt from the water softener, is it because there's too much salt? I still don't know what it is and feel uneasy. I've applied for after-sales service, but I'll write down the reason once it's resolved!

Sentence (English): You have no idea how many YouTube videos I searched just to buy this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ It's quite convenient. ] || ---------------- || You have no idea how many YouTube videos I searched just to buy this dishwasher. Since it's something you use for a long time once you buy it, I read the reviews incredibly thoroughly. I agonized over whether to go with SK or LG. After seeing moisture build up and leak out the sides of other brands, I felt it was a chronic issue with those brands, so I ultimately decided to go with LG. The advantages I saw in LG were the soaking function, high-pressure washing, high-temperature drying, and the water softening function. Today, I tried using it without the water softening function. I pre-washed all the food residue off the dishes before putting them in. The pots, plates, and lids at the very bottom cleaned very well, but in the middle layer, some rice bowls had dried-out rice grains that wouldn't come off. The cutlery was clean, but the dried food residue on the cooking utensils didn't come off either. Also, perhaps because I didn't use the water softening function, there were water stains. Anyway, you have no idea how convenient it is not to have to stand and wash dishes for 30 minutes. Just that alone makes me think I made the right purchase. Next time, I plan to arrange the dishes better and wash them more thoroughly! I spent a lot of time agonizing over the color, so I'm posting this for your reference. (Update) Oh, come to think of it, I've seen newer models come with a frying pan holder. This one doesn't have one; is that because it's an older model? Also, after using it a few times, this white residue remains. Since other regular dishes are transparent or white, it doesn't show well, but it is very noticeable on the frying pan. It washes off easily with water, so I don't think it's limescale. Could it be detergent residue or salt from the water softening process? If it is salt from the softening process, is it because too much salt came out? I still don't know what it is, so it feels a bit unsettling. I have applied for an AS (after-sales service) request, though. I will write down the reason once it is resolved! (Update) After using it for a little over a year, the screen started flickering and making a closing sound as if it wasn't closed properly. I contacted the AS center, and they said the free warranty period had expired and I would have to pay for the repair. Since it only happened occasionally, I just kept using it for now. Exactly two years later, the screen completely broke. Sigh. It wasn't a cheap item that cost just a penny, but the repair cost came out to a fortune. I watched tons of YouTube reviews before buying this dishwasher, but unless you pre-wash the dishes, not a single grain of rice or anything comes out. Anyone who has used a dishwasher in places like the US knows what I'm talking about. You know that even if you just throw everything in haphazardly, it comes out super clean. My LG air conditioner broke down after only two years, so I guess they just do a ton of marketing. I was fooled by the ads and bought it, and now I’m turning my back on them, thinking, "Of course." I mean, I’ve never had any problems with Company S products before, but when I bought this house, I got everything LG, and now the washing machine, dishwasher, and air conditioner are all broken. It’s awful, and I’m so angry!

Sentence (English): I agonized over whether to go with SK or LG.
Comments (English): [ It's quite convenient. ] || ---------------- || You have no idea how many YouTube videos I searched just to buy this dishwasher. Since it's something you use for a long time once you buy it, I read the reviews incredibly thoroughly. I agonized over whether to go with SK or LG. After seeing moisture build up and leak out the sides of other brands, I felt it was a chronic issue with those brands, so I ultimately decided to go with LG. The advantages I saw in LG were the soaking function, high-pressure washing, high-temperature drying, and the water softening function. Today, I tried using it without the water softening function. I pre-washed all the food residue off the dishes before putting them in. The pots, plates, and lids at the very bottom cleaned very well, but in the middle layer, some rice bowls had dried-out rice grains that wouldn't come off. The cutlery was clean, but the dried food residue on the cooking utensils didn't come off either. Also, perhaps because I didn't use the water softening function, there were water stains. Anyway, you have no idea how convenient it is not to have to stand and wash dishes for 30 minutes. Just that alone makes me think I made the right purchase. Next time, I plan to arrange the dishes better and wash them more thoroughly! I spent a lot of time agonizing over the color, so I'm posting this for your reference. (Update) Oh, come to think of it, I've seen newer models come with a frying pan holder. This one doesn't have one; is that because it's an older model? Also, after using it a few times, this white residue remains. Since other regular dishes are transparent or white, it doesn't show well, but it is very noticeable on the frying pan. It washes off easily with water, so I don't think it's limescale. Could it be detergent residue or salt from the water softening process? If it is salt from the softening process, is it because too much salt came out? I still don't know what it is, so it feels a bit unsettling. I have applied for an AS (after-sales service) request, though. I will write down the reason once it is resolved! (Update) After using it for a little over a year, the screen started flickering and making a closing sound as if it wasn't closed properly. I contacted the AS center, and they said the free warranty period had expired and I would have to pay for the repair. Since it only happened occasionally, I just kept using it for now. Exactly two years later, the screen completely broke. Sigh. It wasn't a cheap item that cost just a penny, but the repair cost came out to a fortune. I watched tons of YouTube reviews before buying this dishwasher, but unless you pre-wash the dishes, not a single grain of rice or anything comes out. Anyone who has used a dishwasher in places like the US knows what I'm talking about. You know that even if you just throw everything in haphazardly, it comes out super clean. My LG air conditioner broke down after only two years, so I guess they just do a ton of marketing. I was fooled by the ads and bought it, and now I’m turning my back on them, thinking, "Of course." I mean, I’ve never had any problems with Company S products before, but when I bought this house, I got everything LG, and now the washing machine, dishwasher, and air conditioner are all broken. It’s awful, and I’m so angry!

After seeing moisture build up and leak out the sides of other brands, I felt it was a chronic issue with those brands, so I ultimately decided to go with LG. The advantages I saw in LG were the soaking function, high-pressure washing, high-temperature drying, and the water softening function. Today, I tried using it without the water softening function. I pre-washed all the food residue off the dishes before putting them in. The pots, plates, and lids at the very bottom cleaned very well, but in the middle layer, some rice bowls had dried-out rice grains that wouldn't come off. The cutlery was clean, but the dried food residue on the cooking utensils didn't come off either. Also, perhaps because I didn't use the water softening function, there were water stains. Anyway, you have no idea how convenient it is not to have to stand and wash dishes for 30 minutes. Just that alone makes me think I made the right purchase. Next time, I plan to arrange the dishes better and wash them more thoroughly! I spent a lot of time agonizing over the color, so I'm posting this for your reference. (Update) Oh, come to think of it, I've seen newer models come with a frying pan holder. This one doesn't have one; is that because it's an older model? Also, after using it a few times, this white residue remains. Since other regular dishes are transparent or white, it doesn't show well, but it is very noticeable on the frying pan. It washes off easily with water, so I don't think it's limescale. Could it be detergent residue or salt from the water softening process? If it is salt from the softening process, is it because too much salt came out? I still don't know what it is, so it feels a bit unsettling. I have applied for an AS (after-sales service) request, though. I will write down the reason once it is resolved! (Update) After using it for a little over a year, the screen started flickering and making a closing sound as if it wasn't closed properly. I contacted the AS center, and they said the free warranty period had expired and I would have to pay for the repair. Since it only happened occasionally, I just kept using it for now. Exactly two years later, the screen completely broke. Sigh. It wasn't a cheap item that cost just a penny, but the repair cost came out to a fortune. I watched tons of YouTube reviews before buying this dishwasher, but unless you pre-wash the dishes, not a single grain of rice or anything comes out. Anyone who has used a dishwasher in places like the US knows what I'm talking about. You know that even if you just throw everything in haphazardly, it comes out super clean. My LG air conditioner broke down after only two years, so I guess they just do a ton of marketing. I was fooled by the ads and bought it, and now I’m turning my back on them, thinking, "Of course." I mean, I’ve never had any problems with Company S products before, but when I bought this house, I got everything LG, and now the washing machine, dishwasher, and air conditioner are all broken. It’s awful, and I’m so angry!

Comments (English): [ It's quite convenient. ] || ---------------- || You have no idea how many YouTube videos I searched just to buy this dishwasher. Since it's something you use for a long time once you buy it, I read the reviews incredibly thoroughly. I agonized over whether to go with SK or LG. After seeing moisture build up and leak out the sides of other brands, I felt it was a chronic issue with those brands, so I ultimately decided to go with LG. The advantages I saw in LG were the soaking function, high-pressure washing, high-temperature drying, and the water softening function. Today, I tried using it without the water softening function. I pre-washed all the food residue off the dishes before putting them in. The pots, plates, and lids at the very bottom cleaned very well, but in the middle layer, some rice bowls had dried-out rice grains that wouldn't come off. The cutlery was clean, but the dried food residue on the cooking utensils didn't come off either. Also, perhaps because I didn't use the water softening function, there were water stains. Anyway, you have no idea how convenient it is not to have to stand and wash dishes for 30 minutes. Just that alone makes me think I made the right purchase. Next time, I plan to arrange the dishes better and wash them more thoroughly! I spent a lot of time agonizing over the color, so I'm posting this for your reference. (Update) Oh, come to think of it, I've seen newer models come with a frying pan holder. This one doesn't have one; is that because it's an older model? Also, after using it a few times, this white residue remains. Since other regular dishes are transparent or white, it doesn't show well, but it is very noticeable on the frying pan. It washes off easily with water, so I don't think it's limescale. Could it be detergent residue or salt from the water softening process? If it is salt from the softening process, is it because too much salt came out? I still don't know what it is, so it feels a bit unsettling. I have applied for an AS (after-sales service) request, though. I will write down the reason once it is resolved! (Update) After using it for a little over a year, the screen started flickering and making a closing sound as if it wasn't closed properly. I contacted the AS center, and they said the free warranty period had expired and I would have to pay for the repair. Since it only happened occasionally, I just kept using it for now. Exactly two years later, the screen completely broke. Sigh. It wasn't a cheap item that cost just a penny, but the repair cost came out to a fortune. I watched tons of YouTube reviews before buying this dishwasher, but unless you pre-wash the dishes, not a single grain of rice or anything comes out. Anyone who has used a dishwasher in places like the US knows what I'm talking about. You know that even if you just throw everything in haphazardly, it comes out super clean. My LG air conditioner broke down after only two years, so I guess they just do a ton of marketing. I was fooled by the ads and bought it, and now I’m turning my back on them, thinking, "Of course." I mean, I’ve never had any problems with Company S products before, but when I bought this house, I got everything LG, and now the washing machine, dishwasher, and air conditioner are all broken. It’s awful, and I’m so angry!

I can't say enough about this dishwasher, perhaps because my previous Frigidaire was a piece of crap; I think I would still love it regardless. Highly recommend this LG dishwasher!

Comments (English): [ 1 Month - LOVE IT! ] || ---------------- || We have had this LG dishwasher for a month now - and absolutely LOVE it! The LG is QUIET! I barely hear it running and I am 10 feet from it. It also does an absolutely amazing job at cleaning - and after I have teenagers doing dishes, so after a couple of weeks of no dishwasher, yeah, you can say \"STUCK ON! \". I love the different modes it has, especially its \"Turbo\" which, in an hour, cleans the toughest dishes, all three shelves. I wasn't sure I would use or even like the 3rd top rack, but it is so very useful for utensils and odd shaped items, like Kitchenaid tools. So far, we love it. Sentence (English): The pros: This was very easy to install myself (I am handy, but not an expert by any means).
Comments (English): [ 1 month in, cleans and dries exceptionally ] || ---------------- || The pros: This was very easy to install myself (I am handy, but not an expert by any means). The method it uses to level the front/back/ and left-right feet is genius and easy to do post-installation from the front of the unit. This model cleans dishes exceptionally. I've had zero issues with drying. The flexibility of the racks and tings is convenient. Super quiet operation. The filter is easy to access and clean, and the settings are simple and straight forward. Note that the Crystal Dry function is more aggressive on delicate dishes so I never use it. Even without using crystal dry, the loads are always dry when done. I love the utensil rack on the top it feels like a game changer. Cons: The QR codes in the manual that are supposed to take you to video instructions of each step did not work at the time I installed it. I was disappointed that although the tub is stainless, that the racks and sprayer arms are plastic. I bought the highest model bc I wanted stainless for longevity but also because I worry about micro plastics getting into water supply over time and use. One of the brackets that came with the bosch broke during install when I tried to rebend it. They were much thinner than the brackets that I'd removed from the other brand that I took out. The steel housing of the model in general seems of lesser quality and thinner gauge than the 7 year old kitchen aid dishwasher that the Bosch replaced. I'm afraid that may be a sign of an industry trend in general but I worry about it standing the test of time and abuse

The Auto air feature is awesome so you don't have stuffy smelling utensils nor do you heat up too much to dry. The door pops open, the steam vents out and the heat within helps dry out the utensils perfectly.The red light indicator is fantastic to show it is in use. The clean exterior means no accidental bumping the buttons or panel. The only complaint is that the fron is not fingerprint resistant and so you need to wipe it often

Sentence (English): I'm looking into buying a dishwasher.
Comments (English): I'm looking into buying a dishwasher. There's no room for a 12-person dishwasher in our kitchen, so I decided to get a 6-person dishwasher. I looked at all the other brands, but LG was the best, so I bought it. Since I have a small family, I run it once a day, or maybe twice. I'm 90% free from washing dishes. It's a little noisy, but it's not annoying, and it washes well. I wish the 6-person dishwasher had an automatic door opener. That's a bit disappointing.
Comments (Original): 식기세척기 구매하고 싶어서 알아보는데.12인용은 저희 부엌엔 둘 자리가 없어서 6인용으로 마음먹고 다른 브랜드도 다 찾아봤는데 LG가 제일 마음에 들어 엘지로 구매했습니다.식구가 적어서 하루 한번에서 많으면 두번 정도 돌리게 되네요.설거지에서 90%해방 됐습니다.소음이 좀 있지만 거슬릴 정도는 아니고 세척도 잘 됩니다.6인용 식세기에도 자동문열림 있었으면 좋겠어요. 그게 좀 아쉬워요.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher does not have the drying features that the website says it has.
Comments (English): [ Do Not Buy This Dishwasher if you want dry dishes ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher does not have the drying features that the website says it has. Under product details it reads: Heated Dry Dishwasher - designed with a highly-effective heated dry cycle, this dishwasher consistently delivers completely dry dishes. It also says Dry Boost: Get hard-to-dry items up to 3 times drier than a standard heated dry with this specialized dry cycle. Our dishwasher was old and started leaking, so we had to purchase a new one. After looking at several dishwashers, we chose this one, as well as the 3 year protection plan. We had it delivered and ran it a few times, thinking something was broken, as it was not drying our dishes. The dishwasher was wet inside after the was cycle was completed. So my husband looked at it first and said the heating element is heating when the water is coming in, but it isn't heating after the water is done. So we made a claim for a technician to come out and look at it. He comes over and looks at it for a bit, then tells me that the dishwasher we have has a ventless drying system. He said you do not have the vent in the front that heat would come out of, your model vents through the fill funnel and beach gasket. I told him that is not what the Home Dept website says under the product details. He told me that you need to look at the specific model number and the GE manual, which will show what that model can do. I do not see that manual paired with this dishwasher on The Home Depot site. I do see where it tells me that the dishwasher that I purchased should be drying my dishes. We called our local Home Depot, and because it had been over 48 hours since our purchase, they will not exchange or return our purchase. So be very careful when you are purchasing any appliance with Home Depot, as the description may not accurately describe what you are about to purchase, and if you do not discover within 48 hours that there is a problem, you will not be able to return it. We called our local Home Depot and left messages for the Manager of the appliance department with no return phone calls. I never knew that buying a dishwasher could be such a hot mess.

I love the 3rd rack and flexibility of the interior. This dishwasher cleans well. BUT it is not silent or even quiet. I have single sided deafness and diminished hearing in the other ear. Whirlpool repairman came out and said it was within noise limit and this model tends to be a little noisier. In my opinion no excuse for that at this price level. I struggled with whether to keep this or not. I hope I don't regret it. Sentence (English): The tableware is easy to display and clean.
Comments (English): The tableware is easy to display and clean. Occasionally there are pot bottoms and some dishes that have not been washed. It is understandable. It is much better than hand washing, and it is easier to use than a washing machine. I use it every day. The family is also happy, so there is no need to talk about it. No one needs to do the washing. There is a dishwasher, but it takes a long time to wash, but they use electricity for the dishwashing cycle, and it feels okay. It’s about one kilowatt-hour to two kilowatts at a time, depending on the choice. In addition to the quick wash, the dishwashing time is usually two and a half to four hours, and drying is also added, so unless it is quick wash, it has to be washed once a day, because one day I use it after lunch at noon In order to strengthen washing + drying, the meal is ready at 6 o'clock in the evening, and the dishes have not been washed, but in general it does not affect it, just wash it after dinner. In addition, you can make an appointment to wash, and the electricity fee is cheaper after 11:00 in the evening
Comments (Original): 餐具好摆放，洗的也干净，偶尔有锅底和某些碗筷没洗到也能理解，比手洗好多了，比洗衣机还好用，每天都要用，家里人也高兴了，不用谈论让谁去洗了，谁也不用洗，有洗碗机就是洗得时间有点久，但是他们是洗碗周期用电量，感觉也还行，差不多就是一次一度电到两度电，看选择的模式，除了快洗，一般都是两个半小时到四个小时的洗碗时间，还要加烘干，所以除非快洗，不然都得一天洗一次，因为有天中午我吃完饭一点用了加强洗+烘干，晚上六点饭好了，碗还没洗好，不过总得来说不影响，就晚饭后洗就可以了。另外还可以预约洗，晚上十一点后电费便宜

Sentence (English): I received it and have used it exactly twice.
Comments (English): [ It seems like it doesn't dry very well. ] || ---------------- || I received it and have used it exactly twice. The noise isn't particularly loud, but the sound of the door opening seems a bit loud; I was actually startled. Also, it is bulkier than I expected. Since I live in a rented apartment, I was looking for a no-drill model. It looks a bit messy because of the hose, but I bought it just to use it since my arm hurts. I've run it twice, but it feels like it isn't drying as well. Maybe it's because it uses residual heat for drying. Other reviews show it drying well. I'm not sure if I put it in incorrectly or what, but I'll have to use it more to find out. I will post an updated review regarding the drying process after using it a bit more. Oh, and it takes less water than I expected. I'm not sure if it was cleaned properly, but the amount of water used is less than I anticipated. The amount in the photo is the water remaining after running it once. I've been using it for about a month since purchasing it, and I'm fairly satisfied. If you run it with ceramic dishes without stacking them too much, it does function as a dryer. However, since we have a large family, I can't just put in a small amount, so I stack them up and run it, then take them out to a drying rack to dry afterwards. I think it's better than not having one at all. At first, I thought the sound of the door opening was a bit loud, but I guess I've gotten used to it after using it for a while; it's fine now. However, since my house is small and the living room and kitchen are combined, I do notice some noise when the dishwasher is running. I even ran it late at night around 8 PM, but the sound wasn't extremely bothersome. Comments (English): [ Still learning ] || ---------------- || Did extensive reviews of all makes and models in all price ranges. Due to the high rated reviews of the Bosch brand, I purchased the Bosch 100 model. I've had this dishwasher 4 weeks. I'm not as impressed as I thought I'd be. I cannot load near as many dishes in the dishwasher as I could my old one. The times are restrictive as to what you can put where. I loaded up the silverware baskets like I normally do and the table knives still had the small amount of peanut butter (a smear of pb) on them. Greasy film noted still on plastic wear on top shelf after going thru 60 minute speed cycle. Slightly dried on mashed potatoes still on fork tines after run thru 1 cycle. I'm using the recommended soap and rinse agent and we have good quality well water. Installation booklet was simple and easy to understand but we still had to replace all tubing and electrical cords to make it work. There was no new user booklet that instructed you how to load racks for best results, when to use the 3 different wash cycles, etc. New owner was referred to a website. I like to know how to get the best results out of my new equipment so I'm a happy with my purchase. Another thing I noted was the dishwasher developed an old food smell after the first wash and has not gone away. This was a complaint stated in several reviews. Supposedly a clogged filter is the cause but how could it be clogged with the first load? The dishes were only lightly soiled. Good things about the machine is it's a very quiet washer and the look of the front door and cycle buttons are very sleek.

As the reviews say, it's definitely noisy. (I think it will be difficult to turn in the late evening. Please refer to the sound in the video). I'll have to come back later in the evening. I have a baby, so I need a baby bottle, tableware, etc. I'm really looking forward to the hot water sterilization function. I guess I'll have to use it in the future to see if it cleans well. Good write up thank you!

Sentence (English): It cleans the dishes well enough, which is the main objective.
Comments (English): [ Not terrible, but not great. ] || ---------------- || It cleans the dishes well enough, which is the main objective. Given a choice, however, I would not buy this model again. Several reasons. The top rack is poorly designed. Items placed in it tend to fall over when you slide the rack in and out. Further it lacks the little cup shelves that some models have that fold up or down on the top rack for additional short items. Also a problem: the soap dish has a poorly designed little cover. When you try to close it after putting in soap it often pops right open. Takes several tries to get it to stay closed. I bought this model only because it was the only one I could find in any nearby store available in stock with a white front. I can't really rate dry quality because I never let it dry. When it is done washing I open the door--surprise! the dishes dry! Saves energy.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher ran fine for three cycles, then stopped working.
Comments (English): [ The dishwasher ran fine for three cycles, then stopped working.  ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher ran fine for three cycles, then stopped working. The problem was that the inner surface of the dishwasher has warped, and the feature in the door intended to be the latch/interlock would no longer go into the interlock (it went underneath instead). A repair person was called, and they came out and simply pushed hard on the warped surface to "bend" it back so the interlock would function. She said this wasn't unusual. The only consolation was that she said she'd never been called back out for a repeat issue. This either means the residual stress in the plastic has now been relieved by the heat from the wash/dry cycles, or the owners have learned how to handle it themselves. Somewhat disappointing that this sort of service was needed after literally a week of ownership.

In the co-op where I live, there seemed to be constant leaks and repairs being done on the dishwashers of neighbours. I didn't want to suffer the same fate. When we had the dishwasher installed, I asked the handyman we hired if we should avoid putting a kick plate in front -- although aesthetically pleasing, it would make it harder if the machine needed repairing. The installer said, "It's a Bosch! It's not going to need repairing." Seems he was right. It's been 3 years now and this dishwasher works as beautifully as the day it was first installed. It cleans very well and it's quiet. What more could I ask for?

Comments (English): [ March 2023 ] || ---------------- || This washer cleans and dries great. It's also super quiet. The rack setup takes a little getting use to, but I'm learning to maximize the number of items I can put in it. I use the top flat rack less than I thought I would, but that's mostly because I put all my silverware in the bottom rack baskets. Also, I learned that the middle rack has a higher clearance on the far right side than the far left, so some tall glasses won't fit on the far left. Not a problem, just a note.Areas for improvement: I've discovered that large Chinese food soup containers don't fit in the middle rack because the upper rack hits them. Sentence (English): I've been without a dishwasher for 4 or 5 years because I got sick of buying dishwashers that didn't really work.
Comments (English): [ Very quiet, cleans well ] || ---------------- || I've been without a dishwasher for 4 or 5 years because I got sick of buying dishwashers that didn't really work. Finally, I decided to take a chance on this Bosch. The first thing I noticed is that it's super quiet. In my small house, the kitchen is directly next to (and open to) the living room. But when the dishwasher is running, we barely notice it. We can have a comfortable conversation or watch TV while it's on - no problem.And, as long as I place the dishes in properly, THE DISHES COME OUT CLEAN! I don't pre-wash my dishes at all; I just scrape off chunks of food. Many things sit, dirty, in the dishwasher all day before I run the machine at night. They all come clean! I do occasionally get an error message when the machine is in the drying mode, but it doesn't seem to affect anything. The dishes come out just as dry as they do if I don't get that error message. I'm also trying to adjust to the way the prongs are laid out in the dishwasher; it's different from any machine I've used before. That's probably part of why the machine cleans so well, though.Overall, I heartily recommend this dishwasher.

I need to check whether there's a technique to the tapping required □□Overall, great unit, very happy with the choice!

Sentence (English): I purposely sought out a Kitchenaid dishwasher when our 20-year-old one died in January.
Comments (English): [ Leaking, broken, waste of money ] || ---------------- || I purposely sought out a Kitchenaid dishwasher when our 20-year-old one died in January. I ordered it online site-unseen. based on reviews. AWFUL DECISION. The dishwasher was back-ordered 30 days. ok fine. We finally received it. A week later, we finally found someone to help us install it. We noticed 2 problems immediately. the bottom right foot was bent, and the top rack had a wheel broken off and laying at the bottom of the washer. The first time we turned it on, seconds later, a stream of water came from under the machine! There is a drip pan under the machine, but the water wasn't coming from what would drip into the pan. My husband used a camera on the end of a wire and could see water dripping from nowhere near any of the connected pipes. Back to handwashing again. Called KitchenAid (which is also Whirlpool), they had a repair guy call us to set up a 4-hour window to fix it. Guy shows up the following week, husband fills him in, guy says the "part" is on backorder. Calls back 2 weeks later, part is in. not leaking anymore in the repair guy's word "for now". BUT. the repair guy took off the bracket that came with the washer, said it was the wrong one, but didn't anchor it back down, so now we have to figure out how to anchor it back down. So now, I am scared to use it, still waiting for the replacement top rack, and awaiting home insurance on the real wood floors that have water damage from the original leak. Even the repair guy was shocked at the amount this mostly-plastic machine is made of. Worst, most expensive, house damaging, hours lost at work for the 4-hour windows of repair, pile of plastic we have ever bought. Our loyalty to KitchenAid has ended. Also, for anyone sitting on the fence about buying this machine. I encourage you to check/know 2 things. 1- the big-box home improvement store we bought our machine from. we found out later, only accepts returns for 48 hours and please check reviews for other people's experiences with customer service as part of your research. If you buy this machine, I hope your experience is much better than ours. Totally regretting our purchase.

I was apprehensive about having the controls hidden on the top edge rather than exposed on the front, but in practice this has not been an issue. We use the auto setting almost all the time, and start the dishwasher in the night so we don't miss seeing a count down timer . The stainless steel finish is a fingerprint magnet but does wipe clean. I'm surprised how much I can pack into a load - it's very well organized inside, including the cutlery baskets and the extra drawer on the top for long flat objects. Follow the loading guide in the manual for best results. Again, feels like much more capacity and organization than my previous unit. One nit - the switch to turn it on feels a bit balky/non responsive - have to tap/press it multiple times. I need to check whether there's a technique to the tapping required □□ Overall, great unit, very happy with the choice!

Comments (English): [ Very quiet, cleans well ] || ---------------- || I've been without a dishwasher for 4 or 5 years because I got sick of buying dishwashers that didn't really work. Finally, I decided to take a chance on this Bosch. The first thing I noticed is that it's super quiet. In my small house, the kitchen is directly next to (and open to) the living room. But when the dishwasher is running, we barely notice it. We can have a comfortable conversation or watch TV while it's on - no problem. And, as long as I place the dishes in properly, THE DISHES COME OUT CLEAN! I don't pre-wash my dishes at all; I just scrape off chunks of food. Many things sit, dirty, in the dishwasher all day before I run the machine at night. They all come clean! I do occasionally get an error message when the machine is in the drying mode, but it doesn't seem to affect anything. The dishes come out just as dry as they do if I don't get that error message. I'm also trying to adjust to the way the prongs are laid out in the dishwasher; it's different from any machine I've used before. That's probably part of why the machine cleans so well, though. Overall, I heartily recommend this dishwasher.

Sentence (English): I really like this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher! ] || ---------------- || I really like this dishwasher. It is nice looking & extremely quiet. We picked this one based on how quiet it was & the interior area (rack design & interior space). It has a very easy touch control panel. You just barely touch it & the option is selected. It also does not have an outer handle that sticks out beyond the machine itself. The stainless-steel finish also looks very nice. A few things that would make this even better are: 1) Having a utensil bin attached to the inside of the door. Most utensil bins take up a large area of space on the bottom rack & therefore, useable space is limited. The utensil bin that came with this dishwasher is huge, so I just used my old one to save space. There are also no attachments so it could fit on the door interior as an option. The bin was also one large bin. I thought it might come apart in the middle so you could only use half if you needed, but that was not the case. It was all or nothing. 2) I wish the 3rd upper rack was adjustable. The middle rack is (maybe an inch or two), but the very top rack for utensils, wooden spoons, spatulas etc. is not adjustable so it limits what you can put on that rack because it might be too tall or big. I like having a 3rd rack though. 3) It has a 4 hour delay. Maybe a 1, 2 or 4 hour delay option would be nice. This is not major. just something I had on my old dishwasher. 4) I don't know if dishwashers still have disposals in them or not, but this one does not have one. It is probably something designers think is not necessary, but I loved my old one that had a disposal. Now I have to clean out a filter if any food ends up in the dishwasher instead of letting the dishwasher take care of it. 5) One of the reasons we got this dishwasher was because the racks were descent based on the tines & how much stuff you can fit onto the racks. Others we saw had very small-spaced tines or a what we considered a strange or unusable design. Where the very large utensil bin goes is a very large opening. When you take that bin out, there are no tines available in that space so you can use it for additional plates, bowls, etc. It would be nice to have wall to wall tines on the bottom rack, even if you make it so some of them lay down, when necessary, in order to make the bottom rack fully usable for whatever you need it for. Overall, I really do like this dishwasher. I just hope it lasts more than 5 years as most appliances now days do not last as long as they used to. My old one was 23 years old & still working. It was just getting loud & the tines were starting to break.

Sentence (English): Our dishwasher started leaking and shutting down showing error E15.
Comments (English): [ Great-while it lasted, HORRIBLE support from BOSCH ] || ---------------- || Our dishwasher started leaking and shutting down showing error E15. We were hopeful that it could be fixed so we called a technician to look at it and the diagnosis was that the tub has a leak and some rust present which is not fixable. I was very disappointed, as Bosch has the reputation of a good brand, and to have to throw away a dishwasher after 6 years without the possibility of repair was terrible news. I even purchased the extended warranty, which had just ran out, but I expect most things to break and be repairable, rather than be totaled after the first issue. The technician suggested we contact Bosch to inquire about the warranty, which I did. The Bosch website does list a limited lifetime warranty in case the tub breaks so I was hopeful. I called Bosh and was advised that I need to have a Bosch certified technician to take a look at it before further discussion. A week later a Bosh-certified technician came and gave us the same diagnosis, written in a report ($124) which I sent to Bosch. After review Bosh said they will sell me a new one for the factory price which is lower than the store price but I was disappointed that they would not replace it or replace the tub - We have already been several weeks without a dishwasher so I accepted the offer for the new machine at factory price. After some more time Bosh called back and said everything is in order, and the dishwasher will be ready to ship to me 6 month later! I was in shock and indicated as much to them to which the Bosh representative said that they may have a lower grade model series 100 that they could ship right away - I told them I will discuss it with my wife and call back. However, when I called back there was no record of the 100 series offer, and that the only option I had was to wait for 6 months without a dishwasher. I asked to talk to a supervisor, and was told one would call me back right away (as no-one was available), but now several weeks later, the call never came. The dishwasher was great, we liked it until it broke down and we had to dispose of it. The Bosch customer service experience is subpar. Not only did they not provide us with a reasonable offer to replace or fix the dishwasher, but they were not upfront about it from the beginning, we waited a month thinking that they would honor their warranty. I would say that they don't honor the warranty they offer or it is not offered in good faith. How many customers are in a position to wait 6 months for a replacement machine and still have to pay hundreds of dollars.

I even purchased the extended warranty, which had just ran out, but I expect most things to break and be repairable, rather than be totaled after the first issue. Sentence (English): As Bosch says this thing cleans great!
Comments (English): [ Great cleaner, very basic ] || ---------------- || As Bosch says this thing cleans great! I haven't had any problem with dirty dishes since I got it a couple months ago. The machine is very basic and simple. Sometimes when you open it up right after the wash, everything is so warm that the wheels don't want to turn when you're pulling out the drawers, but it's not really a problem. It says it is 50 dB loud and it is very accurate. I held a decibel measure up to it when it's at its loudest and it's accurate. Which is kind of loud if there is nothing going on in your house. But not too bothersome once you get used to it in a week or so. It's very easy to just push the first button and the last button and start it. My two-year-old hasn't quite figured that out yet so we're still good, but it does have a lock feature when he does figure it out. It does seem to go through a lot of the drying agent liquid, but the dishes are drier than I've ever had, with any other machines that I've owned!

Comments (English): [ Understanding our new dishwasher ] || ---------------- || First of all, we like the dishwasher. It has been doing a good job, but we are still learning about its capabilities. The dishwasher is pleasingly quiet while in operation. We like having the controls on the door where we can see them when the machine operates. The sample of Rinse Aid that came with the dishwasher was in a plastic bag. I could not control it while filling the dispenser. I suggest that if you provide a sample, put it in a bottle. It took me some time to determine how to change the settings for drying and power. (pages 30 – 33) However, when my son said that his Bosch dishwasher power stays on a long time after the cycle finishes, I was able to show him how to limit that to 1 minute. We haven't been able to understand how to use the “cup shelves” (p21 of the manual.) The instructions say to bend them toward the center of the machine until they click. But we could find no way to make them click. So, we have removed them from the rack.
